sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Boone County?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Boone County Assessor sets values, and the Boone County Collector mails the bills and takes the payments. The Collector sits in Room 118 of the Boone County Government Center, at the southwest corner of Ninth and Ash streets in Columbia, and answers at (573) 886-4285 from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

The county covers 691 square miles in the middle of the state, with the Missouri River forming its southern edge. Columbia is the seat and by far the largest city. Ashland, Centralia, Hallsville, Rocheport and Sturgeon are the other incorporated cities, and Harrisburg, Hartsburg, Huntsdale, McBaine and Pierpont are villages. Wherever a house sits, the same two county offices handle the bill, though the school district and city levies behind it differ from one address to the next.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Boone County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists 84,371 housing units for Boone County in 2025 and a population estimate of 191,746. Owners occupy 57.7 percent of homes, a modest share that fits a university town with a large renter base. The University of Missouri, Columbia College and Stephens College all sit in Columbia.

  • Typical home worth, 2020-2024 survey period: $272,800
  • Median household income: $72,758
  • Median gross rent: $1,088 a month
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 787
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 51.5 percent

At the 19 percent residential rate listed on the Collector's site, a $272,800 house carries an assessed value of about $51,832 before any levy is applied.

sections.h2: When is the Boone County real estate tax bill due?
sections.html:
The bill is due when it arrives and no later than December 31. The Collector mails statements during November, and anyone who has not received one by December 10 should call the office. A missing bill does not cancel the tax or the late charges.

Mailed payments count as timely when the postmark is December 31 or earlier. The Collector's FAQ suggests mailing several days ahead, because a mail drop box does not always get a same-day postmark. A drop box under the shelter at the Ninth Street entrance accepts payments until midnight on December 31. State law backs the postmark rule in RSMo 139.100.

Late charges begin in January and rise on the first day of each month until the bill is paid, according to the Collector's FAQ. For land that reaches the back tax book, RSMo 140.100 adds a penalty of 18 percent of the year's delinquency, capped at 2 percent per month when the owner redeems before the sale.

sections.h2: What are the key Boone County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Important Dates page and the Collector's pages give the calendar below. The 2026 appeal deadline has already passed, so a homeowner who missed it should plan for the next cycle.

Boone County dates from the Assessor and Collector pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Property is assessed as it exists on this day
Mid April to early MayNotices of real estate assessment go out
Late April to mid JuneInformal hearings with the Assessor
July 1Assessor certifies the tax rolls
Second Monday in JulyBoard of Equalization filing deadline (July 13 in 2026, now past)
September 30State Tax Commission deadline, or 30 days after the board decision
NovemberCollector mails tax bills
December 31Last day to pay or postmark without late charges
Fourth Monday in AugustDelinquent tax sale on the courthouse steps at 10:00 AM

sections.h2: What if my Boone County assessment looks too high?
sections.html:
The county describes three steps, and each one needs to be done in order.

  • Call or visit the Assessor soon after the notice arrives. An informal meeting explains how the value was built and often settles the question.
  • If that fails, file the Board of Equalization appeal form with the County Clerk, postmarked by the second Monday in July unless the board extends the date.
  • Appeal the board's decision to the Missouri State Tax Commission by September 30 or one month after the decision letter, whichever falls later.

RSMo 138.430 gives owners the right to take that last step. The State Tax Commission also explains that an owner who wants to dispute value can pay the full bill by December 31, write "paid under protest" on the check, and file a written statement with the Collector giving a claimed market value. Missing the appeal window means waiting until the following year to challenge the number.

sections.h2: Can I pay the Boone County tax bill monthly?
sections.html:
Yes. The Collector runs an installment plan for real estate taxes and for Neighborhood Improvement District assessments. To enroll, the current bill has to be paid up. Monthly payments are based on the previous year's base tax divided by the months left in the year, so a plan that starts in March splits the base over ten payments.

The December payment is adjusted to match the current year's bill, and the balance has to clear by December 31 to avoid late fees or termination of the plan. Payment can come by coupon with cash, check or money order, by bank debit on the 5th or 20th, or by credit card on the 20th with a 2.3 percent charge added.

sections.h2: How do escrowed taxes work in Boone County?
sections.html:
If a lender collects tax money with your monthly mortgage payment, the lender asks the Collector for your bill and pays it for you. When the lender asked for the bill before October 1, the Collector sends the owner an informational statement marked as requested by the lien holder. A bill that does not carry that note should go to the mortgage company right away so it can be paid on time.

The responsibility still sits with the owner. The Collector's FAQ says unpaid real estate bills accrue penalties after December 31 even when a servicer was supposed to pay them, so an owner with a new servicer or a paid-off loan should confirm where the bill is going. A homeowner without escrow can pay straight from the informational statement.

sections.h2: Who owes the Boone County tax after a sale closes?
sections.html:
The tax is a lien on the real estate, and the Collector's page states that the new owner is liable for any unpaid taxes after a change in ownership. The same page says buyers are responsible for paying the full bill by December 31, that taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller with a credit to the buyer, and that no money goes to the Collector at the closing table itself.

Timing matters for closings on or after October 1. The bill may still be printed in the seller's name and mailed to the old address unless the buyer tells the Collector or Assessor about the new ownership. Sellers who receive a bill for a house they no longer own should send the new owner's name and address to the Collector. For a house with back taxes, RSMo 140.150 lets the owner pay the delinquent amount, penalty and costs to the Collector at any time before the sale.

faqs.q: When must a Boone County tax bill be paid?
faqs.a: December 31, by receipt or by a postmark dated no later than that day. The Collector mails bills in November, and charges start in January and climb monthly.

faqs.q: Where do I pay in person?
faqs.a: At the Collector's office in Room 118 of the Boone County Government Center in Columbia, open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays. A drop box at the Ninth Street entrance takes payments through midnight on December 31.

faqs.q: Does Boone County sell tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collector's page says the tax certificate sale is held on the fourth Monday in August at 10:00 AM on the courthouse steps for real estate whose taxes remain unpaid.

faqs.q: What did the 2026 Boone County appeal deadline look like?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization deadline was Monday, July 13, 2026, the second Monday in July. That date is past, so the next filing window opens with the following year's assessment notices.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if I never got a bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Boone County's Collector says failure to receive a bill does not relieve the obligation or the late fees. Call (573) 886-4285 if no bill has arrived by December 10.
